entries.input: Prove that $1/\pi$ is the largest real number $a$ for which $a\,x(\pi - x) \leq \sin x$ holds for every $x \in [0, \pi]$.
entries.name: Putnam2025A2Lower
entries.conclusion: IsGreatest {a : ℝ | ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) Real.pi, a * (x * (Real.pi - x)) ≤ Real.sin x} (1 / Real.pi)
entries.title: Putnam 2025 A2, the lower constant
entries.witness_note: The entry has no binders: it states one closed claim about a single set, so there is nothing for A6 to existentially close and a `trivial` witness would record coverage that was never obtained.

entries.input: Prove that $4/\pi^{2}$ is the smallest real number $b$ for which $\sin x \leq b\,x(\pi - x)$ holds for every $x \in [0, \pi]$.
entries.name: Putnam2025A2Upper
entries.conclusion: IsLeast {b : ℝ | ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) Real.pi, Real.sin x ≤ b * (x * (Real.pi - x))} (4 / Real.pi ^ 2)
entries.title: Putnam 2025 A2, the upper constant
entries.witness_note: The entry has no binders: it states one closed claim about a single set, so there is nothing for A6 to existentially close and a `trivial` witness would record coverage that was never obtained.

entries.input: Prove that $4/\pi^{2}$ is the largest real number $a$ for which $a\,x(\pi - x) \leq \sin x$ holds for every $x \in [0, \pi]$.
entries.name: Putnam2025A2LowerTwin
entries.conclusion: IsGreatest {a : ℝ | ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) Real.pi, a * (x * (Real.pi - x)) ≤ Real.sin x} (4 / Real.pi ^ 2)
entries.title: Putnam 2025 A2, the two constants swapped
entries.rationale: A soundness twin for `putnam-2025-a2-lower`: it names the problem's *other* constant. $4/\pi^{2}$ is the value of $\sin x / (x(\pi - x))$ at $x = \pi/2$, where the ratio is largest, so it bounds the quotient above and not below; at $x = 1/10$ the claimed inequality reads $0.1233 \leq 0.0998$. Both constants are in the paper's answer, which is what makes the swap plausible. It states nothing the paper asked, so it cites no occurrence.
entries.witness_note: The entry has no binders: it states one closed claim about a single set, so there is nothing for A6 to existentially close and a `trivial` witness would record coverage that was never obtained.

entries.input: Prove that $480/49$ is the greatest value of $\sum_{i=1}^{10} \cos(3x_i)$ over all real numbers $x_1, \dots, x_{10}$ with $\sum_{i=1}^{10} \cos(x_i) = 0$.
entries.name: Putnam2018A3
entries.conclusion: IsGreatest {t : ℝ | ∃ x : Fin 10 → ℝ, ∑ i, Real.cos (x i) = 0 ∧ ∑ i, Real.cos (3 * x i) = t} (480 / 49)
entries.title: Putnam 2018 A3
entries.witness_note: The entry has no binders: it states one closed claim about a single set, so there is nothing for A6 to existentially close and a `trivial` witness would record coverage that was never obtained.
